ACE3 Ballistics calculator - WCF

Accuracy warning: The source-based muzzle-velocity adjustments, ACE SQF drag tables and atmosphere/stability formulas are implemented. The offline model uses ACE drag tables and an altitude-dependent atmospheric profile, but trajectory parity with live engine physics is not established. The exact in-game wind map, including terrain-dependent wind effects, is not included. Initial speed is estimated from exported weapon and magazine configs; other mods or engine effects may change actual speed.

Load weapon + magazine ballistics

Search the firearms recognized in your loaded Arma 3 + mod configuration. Compatible magazines are resolved from direct weapon entries and CfgMagazineWells. Only ACE bullet projectiles are selectable; mortars, rockets and shells are omitted.

Subsonic data: ACE-processed arrays loaded from preprocessed data. Some labelled subsonic calibers have supersonic velocities, these are treated as if still subsonic as per the game's configuration.

Muzzle compatibility is not accounted for. The selection lists muzzle attachments from all mods, but it cannot verify whether one fits the chosen rifle. Select only an attachment your weapon can equip in Arsenal. Manual muzzle velocity is treated as the final measured speed, without a second attachment multiplier.

No muzzle device selected.
Choose a weapon and magazine.

Attachment MagazineCoef.initSpeed multiplies magazine launch speed before the ACE barrel-length and ammunition-temperature processing; it can be overridden by the ACE velocity table. AmmoCoef.airFriction affects simple-mode drag; ACE G-model drag instead uses the projectile BC. MuzzleCoef.dispersionCoef is applied to probability estimates. Typical speed is displayed for reference, not substituted for muzzle velocity.

The automatic speed starts with magazine initSpeed, applies positive/negative weapon initSpeed rules from ACE's weapon diagnostic function, then applies the exact lookup-table adjustments in the uploaded firing handler. Random velocity variation is intentionally omitted from deterministic predictions. ACE-processed subsonic muzzle-velocity and temperature tables are imported for all subsonic projectiles included in the modlist. CUP subsonic-labelled classes retain the high processed muzzle speeds observed in Arsenal; the class name does not override the in-game configuration.

Saved weapon profiles

Save the selected rifle, ammunition, muzzle device, zero, ballistics and current shooting inputs as an offline preset. Saved profiles stay in this browser when storage is available. Export JSON for backups or to transfer profiles to another device.

Profiles are stored only on this device; use Export JSON to transfer to other devices or backup profiles.

Target and firing geometry

Scope zero is calculated as a level shot in still air using the selected projectile, current atmospheric readings, and sight height; the same in-flight atmosphere setting is used for zero and target shots. Elevation output is the additional correction to dial from that zero. This does not read optic settings from in game.

Projectile and drag

In-game weather measurements

Enter readings from the kestrel, ensuring to get an accurate wind reading. Humidity is entered as a percentage (for example, 50 for 50%).

Clock mode: 12 o’clock = wind from in front (headwind); 6 = behind (tailwind); 3 = from your right (pushes left); 9 = from your left (pushes right). Clock is relative to where you are aiming, not compass north. Each hour is 30°; decimals are allowed for precise directions (e.g. 5.87), this method takes ignores the need for a bearing to target, but is less percise. Compass mode instead uses an absolute wind FROM bearing, will give a wildly inaccurate reading if bearing to target is not entered correctly.

Choose a compass bearing or a wind clock position. Both modes use the same crosswind and head/tailwind calculation.

Altitude-dependent atmosphere uses the Rust extension’s temperature lapse rate (6.5 °C per km) and standard-atmosphere pressure exponent. Pressure is anchored to your measured muzzle pressure, so no map elevation or overcast input is required. Humidity is kept at the entered relative humidity. An optional density override sets the muzzle density and follows the calculated relative changes with height.

Wind FROM bearing and clock direction are converted to the same relative wind vector; zero crosswind correctly occurs for wind directly along the shooting direction. The ATrag-style trajectory solver uses the first wind vector during integration and the second as a separate estimate. Rust native flight has terrain-dependent wind reduction, altitude-dependent weather and engine frame coupling; this standalone page does not reproduce terrain or engine frames.

Optional Advanced Ballistics effects

Scope corrections — mil primary, MOA reference

Results are corrections from the selected optic zero distance, rather than total bullet drop from a horizontal bore. Default mode solves the ATrag-style trajectory using ACE Rust drag and atmospheric correction. Native-inspired drift adds Coriolis and spin accelerations during integration, but cannot exactly reproduce Arma engine frames, terrain-reduced wind. Values below are model predictions, not guaranteed in-game impact adjustments.

Estimated hit probability — mechanical dispersion

This is a gameplay estimate for a perfectly centred, correctly zeroed single shot at the target range above, accounting for the selected weapon's configured random dispersion only. It excludes aiming errors, sway, recoil, wind-reading errors and other sources of misses. Bohemia specifies dispersion in radians but does not establish the exact shot-location probability distribution used here. This is an estimation, not an exact assurance.

Head-sized circle — estimated single-shot probability—10 cm radius
Torso-sized circle — estimated single-shot probability—25 cm radius
Effective dispersion (primary firing mode × device)——
Assumed shot-spread radius at range——

Interpretation: The uniform model assumes equal shot density in a circle of radius range × tan(dispersion). The Gaussian model assumes that same radius encompasses 95% of shots. Neither is a verified Arma engine distribution. These figures are useful for comparing weapons under the chosen model, not guaranteed real in-game hit percentages. The target areas are deliberately simplified circles, not anatomical hitboxes.

Range card

Generate a range table for the selected rifle, load, zero, wind, direction and weather. Each row is calculated with the same trajectory model as the main result. The target inclination is held constant across rows.

The range card is generated locally; no connection to Arma or the internet is required.

Range (m)Elev (mil)Elev (MOA)Wind (mil)Wind 2 (mil)TOF (s)Speed (m/s)

Windage convention: RIGHT positive, LEFT negative. First and second wind columns reflect the currently selected wind layers. Values assume unchanged environmental readings and target bearing.

Output convention: 1 mil = 3.43774677 MOA. Positive elevation is UP, positive windage is RIGHT. Lead is the angular allowance for target speed perpendicular to the line of sight (positive toward the target movement direction). Kinetic energy is ft·lbf. Zero is solved numerically under current weather, still air and level line of sight. The solver uses ACE3 drag data but has not been validated against actual in-game impacts. This is a standalone offline HTML file, not an APK.
